content: A model is a structured representation, plan, or description that is specifically designed to illustrate the structure or functioning of an object, system, or concept. It can also be understood as a scaled-down or simplified version of the actual entity being studied. In the context of abstractions, concepts, and theories: A model in its abstract form refers to a conceptual or theoretical construct used to develop predictive formulas. A causal model is an abstract framework that employs cause-and-effect reasoning to explain relationships. A mathematical model utilizes mathematical language to represent systems or phenomena in an abstract manner. A computer model is a software program designed to simulate an abstract representation of a specific system. A data model describes the structural organization of a database. In economics, a model refers to theoretical frameworks used to analyze economic systems or behaviors. Scientific modeling involves the creation of abstract models to represent and study complex systems or phenomena. An in vitro model replicates biological processes in a controlled environment for research purposes in biology or medicine. Model-Driven Engineering systematically applies models to streamline engineering processes. Molecular modeling employs computational techniques to simulate and predict molecular behavior. Geologic modeling involves the creation of computerized representations of geological features for applied scientific purposes. Morphological modeling is a problem-solving approach used when causal modeling is insufficient or ineffective. The Standard Model in particle physics describes fundamental forces and particles within the universe. Model building in particle physics involves constructing new theoretical frameworks that extend beyond the Standard Model. Meta-modeling refers to the creation of models that describe other models. A business model outlines the operational and financial structure of a business entity. Model theory is the mathematical study of the representation of abstract concepts. Similitude in engineering refers to the use of physical models for scientific testing and validation. A working model in engineering refers to functional software or prototypes used for practical applications. As representations of objects: A physical model is a tangible representation of an object. Solid modeling focuses on creating unambiguous representations of the solid components of an object. A scale model is a smaller or proportional replica of an object, often used as a prototype. Model building as a hobby involves constructing material replicas of objects for recreational purposes. A 3D model is a digital, polygonal representation of an object, typically visualized using computer software. In the context of human and animal behavior: An organism, or a set of signals originating from it, can serve as a model that is imitated by another. For example, a fashion model or promotional model represents a specific standard or ideal that others mimic or follow.
